technique_name: Air Interface Interception Attack > IMSI Interception Attack
description: The request to initiate a real identity verification for a mobile phone is called an "Identity Request." This request requires the mobile phone to provide its real identity, specifically the IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity).
resource_required: srsLTE (open-source LTE SDR software) + USRP (radio frequency equipment)
potential_defenses: 5G decided to introduce the public key and private key mechanism. The public key is used for public disclosure and encryption, and the private key is used for retention and decryption. The public key is stored on the mobile phone, and the private key is stored in the hands of the operator. In this way, only the operator can decrypt the real identity information of the mobile phone, and the attacker can only obtain the encrypted information. Without the private key, the attacker cannot obtain the IMSI.
In this case, what is the authentication process of the entire mobile phone?

In 5G, the real identity of a UE is called a subscription permanent identifier (SUPI) (similar to IMSI). The ciphertext encrypted by the public key is called SUCI (SUbscription Concealed Identifier). After the SUPI is transmitted to the eNodeB, the eNodeB directly uploads the SUPI to the core network.
The public key used by the mobile phone to encrypt the SUPI is stored in the USIM of the UICC.
The SUCI decryption algorithm (SIDF) is executed only once and stored in the UDM of the core network.
